title: Who waits: first reviews by permit type and job size
question: Do big jobs and small jobs, new buildings and alterations, meet the review deadline equally often?
finding: First reviews by permit type and cost band: additions alterations or repairs $5 million and over: 23% on time, median 104 days from filing; new construction $5 million and over: 24% on time, median 114 days from filing; additions alterations or repairs under $10,000: 30% on time, median 77 days from filing; demolitions under $10,000: 28% on time, median 123 days from filing.
how: Finished first reviews of permits filed 2015 to 2026, grouped by the permit type and the cost band in the Building Permits table (revised cost where given, else estimated cost). Groups under 100 reviews are left out.
limits: PermitSF announced these targets in May 2025. Earlier rows are retrospective comparisons. The City set a goal of meeting each calendar-day target on 75% of applicable reviews. Its April 2024 housing guidance used business days, different start events and unit-count thresholds. Bigger jobs pass more stations and need more drawings, so longer waits are expected; the cost on the permit is the applicant’s estimate. Permits filed before 2012 have no cost in the table on disk.
